The output is 4 raw bytes (chain hex:encode), where CyberChef shows hex text.

Two words, the check digit and a validity flag, instead of a three-line report whose "validated string" is not a validation. The radix is a parameter in both (an even number from 2 to 36, default 10). CyberChef's "Checksum" line, the sum modulo the radix of the input as given, is not offered on its own: validate is true when that sum is 0. The check digit is one lowercase character, as in CyberChef. The empty input gives the empty check digit in both; validate is false for it.

Presets by CyberChef's names (all 171, with the same parameters); custom parameters in crc:custom. The output is raw bytes (ceil(width/8) of them), not hex text padded to ceil(width/4) digits. The default is the CRC-32 preset (CyberChef's default is Custom, with width 0), and crc:custom defaults to the CRC-32 parameters (CyberChef's are all 0) and accepts widths of 1 to 82 bits.

Folds the carry until it is gone (RFC 1071), while CyberChef folds it once, so for some inputs (for example the bytes ff ff ff ff 00 01) CyberChef prints "-1" where RFC 1071 gives fffe. The output is 2 raw bytes (chain hex:encode), always four hex digits; CyberChef shows hex text without padding to four digits (0x0f67 shows as "f67"). Confirmed in CyberChef's TCPIPChecksum.mjs: one fold, then Utils.hex(0xffff - csum) with the default padding of 2.

The default blocksize is 4, the same as CyberChef's. The output is blocksize raw bytes (chain hex:encode), where CyberChef shows hex text. A short last block is treated as zero-padded in both. The blocksize is 1 to 65536 in Forge; CyberChef accepts any positive integer.

Two words, encode and decode, instead of an Encode/Decode switch. parity:decode verifies the parity by default (verify=true) and raises E_COERCE on a mismatch or an unexpected character, whereas CyberChef's decode strips the bit without checking; verify=false gives CyberChef's behaviour. The one exception is an empty block between delimiters, for which decode raises E_COERCE ("no parity bit to remove") even with verify=false, where CyberChef returns the empty block. The default position is end, where CyberChef's first (default) Position is Start; the default mode is even in both. Encoding is the same.
